title: ARMA Model
text: Autoregressive-moving-average (ARMA) models provide a parsimonious description of a (weakly) stationary stochastic process in terms of two polynomials, one for the autoregression (AR) and the second for the moving average (MA).

title: Access Mediation
text: Access mediation is the process of granting or denying specific requests to: 1) obtain and use information and related information processing services; and 2) enter specific physical facilities (e.g., Federal buildings, military establishments, border crossing entrances). Access mediation decisions should enforce least privilege by granting access for scoped durations to prevent privilege creep and, where applicable, implement just-in-time (JIT) access. Denial decisions may prevent initial access or terminate access that has already been granted, ensuring continuous enforcement of security policies.

title: Access Modeling
text: Access modeling captures and records the access permissions granted to identities (e.g., administrators, users, groups, systems) and optionally includes details on how these identities are stored, managed, and shared across systems.

title: Access Policy Administration
text: Access policy administration is the systematic process of defining, implementing, and managing access control policies that dictate user permissions to resources.

title: Account Locking
text: The process of temporarily disabling user accounts on a system or domain.

title: Active Certificate Analysis
text: Actively collecting PKI certificates by connecting to the server and downloading its server certificates for analysis.

title: Active Logical Link Mapping
text: Active logical link mapping sends and receives network traffic as a means to map the whole data link layer, where the links represent logical data flows rather than physical connection

title: Active Physical Link Mapping
text: Active physical link mapping sends and receives network traffic as a means to map the physical layer.

title: Administrative Network Activity Analysis
text: Detection of unauthorized use of administrative network protocols by analyzing network activity against a baseline.

title: Agent Authentication
text: Agent authentication is the process of verifying the identities of agents to ensure they are authorized and trustworthy participants within a system.

title: Application-based Process Isolation
text: Application code which prevents its own subroutines from accessing intra-process / internal memory space.

title: Application Configuration Hardening
text: Modifying an application's configuration to reduce its attack surface.

title: Application Exception Monitoring
text: Monitoring the failures of system counters and timers.

title: Application Hardening
text: Application Hardening makes an executable application more resilient to a class of exploits which either introduce new code or execute unwanted existing code. These techniques may be applied at compile-time or on an application binary.

title: Application Performance Monitoring
text: Monitoring the count and duration of the application or program cycle.

title: Application Protocol Command Analysis
text: Analyzing application protocol level remote commands to detect unauthorized activity.

title: Asset Inventory
text: Asset inventorying identifies and records the organization's assets and enriches each inventory item with knowledge about their vulnerabilities.

title: Asset Vulnerability Enumeration
text: Asset vulnerability enumeration enriches inventory items with knowledge identifying their vulnerabilities.

title: Authentication Cache Invalidation
text: Removing tokens or credentials from an authentication cache to prevent further user associated account accesses.

title: Authentication Event Thresholding
text: Collecting authentication events, creating a baseline user profile, and determining whether authentication events are consistent with the baseline profile.

title: Authorization Event Thresholding
text: Collecting authorization events, creating a baseline user profile, and determining whether authorization events are consistent with the baseline profile.

title: Biometric Authentication
text: Using biological measures in order to authenticate a user.

title: Bootloader Authentication
text: Cryptographically authenticating the bootloader software before system boot.

title: Broadcast Domain Isolation
text: Broadcast isolation restricts the number of computers a host can contact on their LAN.

title: Bus Message Authentication
text: Applies cryptographic primitives to individual bus frames to verify the sender's identity and ensure the integrity of the data payload.

title: Byte Sequence Emulation
text: Analyzing sequences of bytes and determining if they likely represent malicious shellcode.

title: Certificate-based Authentication
text: Requiring a digital certificate in order to authenticate a user.

title: Certificate Analysis
text: Analyzing Public Key Infrastructure certificates to detect if they have been misconfigured or spoofed using both network traffic, certificate fields and third-party logs.

title: Certificate Pinning
text: Persisting either a server's X.509 certificate or their public key and comparing that to server's presented identity to allow for greater client confidence in the remote server's identity for SSL connections.

title: Certificate Rotation
text: Certificate rotation involves replacing digital certificates and their private keys to maintain cryptographic integrity and trust, mitigating key compromise risks and ensuring continuous secure communications.

title: Change Default Password
text: Changing the default password means replacing the factory-set credentials with a strong, unique password before the device is deployed, preventing unauthorized access.

title: Client-server Payload Profiling
text: Comparing client-server request and response payloads to a baseline profile to identify outliers.

title: Configuration Inventory
text: Configuration inventory identifies and records the configuration of software and hardware and their components throughout the organization.

title: Connected Honeynet
text: A decoy service, system, or environment, that is connected to the enterprise network, and simulates or emulates certain functionality to the network, without exposing full access to a production system.

title: Connection Attempt Analysis
text: Analyzing failed connections in a network to detect unauthorized activity.

title: Container Image Analysis
text: Analyzing a Container Image with respect to a set of policies.

title: Content Excision
text: Removing specific, potentially malicious, parts of content

title: Content Filtering
text: Content Filtering techniques aid in the process of analyzing an input file for malicious or erroneous content and outputing a sanitized version.

title: Content Format Conversion
text: Content format conversion is mechanical transformation from one format to another which may be normalization or specifically flattening.

title: Content Modification
text: Modify content that does not comply with policy.

title: Content Quarantine
text: Transfer content that does not comply with policy to a quarantine zone.

title: Content Rebuild
text: Rebuild the file according to the spec so any unreferenced components or objects are removed.

title: Content Substitution
text: Modifies specific digital content information by replacing it with something else.

title: Content Validation
text: Verify and validate contents complies with policy

title: Control Flow Integrity
text: Enforcing legal control flow transfers during application process execution.

title: Credential Compromise Scope Analysis
text: Determining which credentials may have been compromised by analyzing the user logon history of a particular system.

title: Credential Eviction
text: Credential Eviction techniques disable or remove compromised credentials from a computer network.

title: Credential Hardening
text: Credential Hardening techniques modify system or network properties in order to protect system or network/domain credentials.

title: Credential Revocation
text: Deleting a set of credentials permanently to prevent them from being used to authenticate.

title: Credential Rotation
text: Credential rotation is a security procedure in which authentication credentials, such as passwords, API keys, or certificates, are regularly changed or replaced to minimize the risk of unauthorized access.

title: Credential Scrubbing
text: The systematic removal of hard-coded credentials from source code to prevent accidental exposure and unauthorized access.

title: Credential Transmission Scoping
text: Limiting the transmission of a credential to a scoped set of relying parties.

title: DNS Allowlisting
text: Permitting only approved domains and their subdomains to be resolved.

title: DNS Cache Eviction
text: Flushing DNS to clear any IP addresses or other DNS records from the cache.

title: DNS Denylisting
text: Blocking DNS Network Traffic based on criteria such as IP address, domain name, or DNS query type.

title: DNS Traffic Analysis
text: Analysis of domain name metadata, including name and DNS records, to determine whether the domain is likely to resolve to an undesirable host.

title: Data Exchange Mapping
text: Data exchange mapping identifies and models the organization's intended design for the flows of the data types, formats, and volumes between systems at the application layer.

title: Data Inventory
text: Data inventorying identifies and records the schemas, formats, volumes, and locations of data stored and used on the organization's architecture.

title: Database Query String Analysis
text: Analyzing database queries to detect [SQL Injection](https://capec.mitre.org/data/definitions/66.html).

title: Dead Code Elimination
text: Removing unreachable or "dead code" from compiled source code.

title: Decoy Environment
text: A Decoy Environment comprises hosts and networks for the purposes of deceiving an attacker.

title: Decoy File
text: A file created for the purposes of deceiving an adversary.

title: Decoy Network Resource
text: Deploying a network resource for the purposes of deceiving an adversary.

title: Decoy Object
text: A Decoy Object is created and deployed for the purposes of deceiving attackers.

title: Decoy Persona
text: Establishing a fake online identity to misdirect, deceive, and or interact with adversaries.

title: Decoy Public Release
text: Issuing publicly released media to deceive adversaries.

title: Decoy Session Token
text: An authentication token created for the purposes of deceiving an adversary.

title: Decoy User Credential
text: A Credential created for the purpose of deceiving an adversary.

title: Direct Physical Link Mapping
text: Direct physical link mapping creates a physical link map by direct observation and recording of the physical network links.

title: Directional Network Link
text: Enforce one-way network communication by preventing two-way communication.

title: Disable Remote Access
text: Limiting access to a computing device which is not required through or from a non-organization-controlled network.

title: Disk Encryption
text: Encrypting a hard disk partition to prevent cleartext access to a file system.

title: Disk Erasure
text: Disk Erasure is the process of securely deleting all data on a disk to ensure that it cannot be recovered by any means.

title: Disk Formatting
text: Disk Formatting is the process of preparing a data storage device, such as a hard drive, solid-state drive, or USB flash drive, for initial use.

title: Disk Partitioning
text: Disk Partitioning is the process of dividing a disk into multiple distinct sections, known as partitions.

title: Domain Account Monitoring
text: Monitoring the existence of or changes to Domain User Accounts.

title: Domain Logic Validation
text: Validation of variable state in the context of the domain application.

title: Domain Name Reputation Analysis
text: Analyzing the reputation of a domain name.

title: Domain Registration Takedown
text: The process of performing a takedown of the attacker's domain registration infrastructure.

title: Domain Trust Policy
text: Restricting inter-domain trust by modifying domain configuration.

title: Driver Load Integrity Checking
text: Ensuring the integrity of drivers loaded during initialization of the operating system.

title: Dynamic Analysis
text: Executing or opening a file in a synthetic "sandbox" environment to determine if the file is a malicious program or if the file exploits another program such as a document reader.

title: Electromagnetic Radiation Hardening
text: The application of physical and material-level design measures to electronic systems, components, or facilities to reduce their susceptibility to damage or disruption from electromagnetic threats.

title: Electronic Lock Monitoring
text: Monitoring electronic lock and door hardware states and access events (e.g., locked/unlocked, access granted/denied, door forced/held, tamper) to detect and respond to unauthorized entry.

title: Email Filtering
text: Filtering incoming email traffic based on specific criteria.

title: Email Removal
text: The email removal technique deletes email files from system storage.

title: Emulated File Analysis
text: Emulating instructions in a file looking for specific patterns.

title: Encrypted Tunnels
text: Encrypted encapsulation of routable network traffic.

title: Endpoint-based Web Server Access Mediation
text: Endpoint-based web server access mediation regulates web server access directly from user endpoints by implementing mechanisms such as client-side certificates and endpoint security software to authenticate devices and ensure compliant access.

title: Endpoint Health Beacon
text: Monitoring the security status of an endpoint by sending periodic messages with health status, where absence of a response may indicate that the endpoint has been compromised.

title: Exception Handler Pointer Validation
text: Validates that a referenced exception handler pointer is a valid exception handler.

title: Executable Allowlisting
text: Using a digital signature to authenticate a file before opening.

title: Executable Denylisting
text: Blocking the execution of files on a host in accordance with defined application policy rules.

title: Execution Isolation
text: Execution Isolation techniques prevent application processes from accessing non-essential system resources, such as memory, devices, or files.

title: File Access Pattern Analysis
text: Analyzing the files accessed by a process to identify unauthorized activity.

title: File Analysis
text: File Analysis is an analytic process to determine a file's status. For example: virus, trojan, benign, malicious, trusted, unauthorized, sensitive, etc.

title: File Carving
text: Identifying and extracting files from network application protocols through the use of network stream reassembly software.

title: File Content Analysis
text: Employing a pattern matching algorithm to statically analyze the content of files.

title: File Content Decompression Checking
text: Checking if compressed or encoded data sections can be successfully decompressed or decoded. Can follow with further analysis with semantic knowledge

title: File Content Rules
text: Employing a pattern matching rule language to analyze the content of files.

title: File Creation Analysis
text: Analyzing the properties of file create system call invocations.

title: File Encryption
text: Encrypting a file using a cryptographic key.

title: File Eviction
text: File eviction techniques delete files from system storage.

title: File Format Verification
text: Verifying that a file conforms to its expected format specifications

title: File Hash Reputation Analysis
text: Analyzing the reputation of a file hash.

title: File Hashing
text: Employing file hash comparisons to detect known malware.

title: File Integrity Monitoring
text: Detecting any suspicious changes to files in a computer system.

title: File Internal Structure Verification
text: The process of checking specific static values within a file, such as file signatures or magic numbers, to ensure they match the expected values defined by the file format specification.

title: File Magic Byte Verification
text: Utilizing the magic number to verify the file

title: File Metadata Consistency Validation
text: The process of validating the consistency between a file's metadata and its actual content, ensuring that elements like declared lengths, pointers, and checksums accurately describe the file's content.

title: File Metadata Value Verification
text: The process of checking specific static values within a file, such as file signatures or magic numbers, to ensure they match the expected values defined by the file format specification.

title: Firmware Behavior Analysis
text: Analyzing the behavior of embedded code in firmware and looking for anomalous behavior and suspicious activity.

title: Firmware Embedded Monitoring Code
text: Monitoring code is injected into firmware for integrity monitoring of firmware and firmware data.

title: Firmware Verification
text: Cryptographically verifying firmware integrity.

title: Forward Resolution Domain Denylisting
text: Blocking a lookup based on the query's domain name value.

title: Forward Resolution IP Denylisting
text: Blocking a DNS lookup's answer's IP address value.

title: Hardware-based Process Isolation
text: Preventing one process from writing to the memory space of another process through hardware based address manager implementations.

title: Hardware-based Write Protection
text: Physical methods of preventing data from being written to computer storage.

title: Hardware Component Inventory
text: Hardware component inventorying identifies and records the hardware items in the organization's architecture.

title: Hierarchical Domain Denylisting
text: Blocking the resolution of any subdomain of a specified domain name.

title: Homoglyph Denylisting
text: Blocking DNS queries that are deceptively similar to legitimate domain names.

title: Homoglyph Detection
text: Comparing strings using a variety of techniques to determine if a deceptive or malicious string is being presented to a user.

title: Host Reboot
text: Initiating a host's reboot sequence to terminate all running processes.

title: Host Shutdown
text: Initiating a host's shutdown sequence to terminate all running processes.

title: IO Port Restriction
text: Limiting access to computer input/output (IO) ports to restrict unauthorized devices.

title: IPC Traffic Analysis
text: Analyzing standard inter process communication (IPC) protocols to detect deviations from normal protocol activity.

title: IP Reputation Analysis
text: Analyzing the reputation of an IP address.

title: Identifier Activity Analysis
text: Taking known malicious identifiers and determining if they are present in a system.

title: Identifier Analysis
text: Analyzing identifier artifacts such as IP address, domain names, or URL(I)s.

title: Identifier Reputation Analysis
text: Analyzing the reputation of an identifier.

title: Inbound Session Volume Analysis
text: Analyzing inbound network session or connection attempt volume.

title: Inbound Traffic Filtering
text: Restricting network traffic originating from untrusted networks destined towards a private host or enclave.

title: Indirect Branch Call Analysis
text: Analyzing vendor specific branch call recording in order to detect ROP style attacks.

title: Input Device Analysis
text: Operating system level mechanisms to prevent abusive input device exploitation.

title: Integer Range Validation
text: Ensuring that an integer is within a valid range.

title: Integrated Honeynet
text: The practice of setting decoys in a production environment to entice interaction from attackers.

title: Job Function Access Pattern Analysis
text: Detecting anomalies in user access patterns by comparing user access activity to behavioral profiles that categorize users by role such as job title, function, department.

title: Kernel-based Process Isolation
text: Using kernel-level capabilities to isolate processes.

title: LAN Access Mediation
text: LAN access mediation encompasses the application of strict access control policies, systematic verification of devices, and authentication mechanisms to govern connectivity to a Local Area Network.

title: Local Account Monitoring
text: Analyzing local user accounts to detect unauthorized activity.

title: Local File Access Mediation
text: Local file access mediation is the process of an operating system granting or denying a specific access request to a local file.

title: Local File Permissions
text: Local file permissions is the systematic process of defining, implementing, and managing access control policies that dictate user permissions for accessing files on a local system through the configuration of operating system functionality.

title: Logical Link Mapping
text: Logical link mapping creates a model of existing or previous node-to-node connections using network-layer data or metadata.

title: Memory Block Start Validation
text: Ensuring that a pointer accurately references the beginning of a designated memory block.

title: Memory Boundary Tracking
text: Analyzing a call stack for return addresses which point to unexpected memory locations.

title: Message Analysis
text: Analyzing email or instant message content to detect unauthorized activity.

title: Message Authentication
text: Authenticating the sender of a message and ensuring message integrity.

title: Message Encryption
text: Encrypting a message body using a cryptographic key.

title: Message Hardening
text: The application of security controls to user-to-user and system-to-system communications so messages remain confidential, unaltered, and verifiable while resisting injection, replay, and tampering.

title: Motion Sensor Monitoring
text: Monitoring events from motion detectors (e.g., passive IR, microwave, dual-technology) to detect presence or movement within protected areas.

title: Multi-factor Authentication
text: Requiring proof of two or more pieces of evidence in order to authenticate a user.

title: Network Access Mediation
text: Network access mediation is the control method for authorizing access to a system by a user (or a process acting on behalf of a user) communicating through a network, including a local area network, a wide area network, and the Internet.

title: Network Isolation
text: Network Isolation techniques prevent network hosts from accessing non-essential system network resources.

title: Network Mapping
text: Network mapping encompasses the techniques to identify and model the physical layer, network layer, and data exchange layers of the organization's network and their physical location, and determine allowed pathways through that network.

title: Network Node Inventory
text: Network node inventorying identifies and records all the network nodes (hosts, routers, switches, firewalls, etc.) in the organization's architecture.

title: Network Resource Access Mediation
text: Control of access to organizational systems and services by users or processes over a network.

title: Network Traffic Analysis
text: Analyzing intercepted or summarized computer network traffic to detect unauthorized activity.

title: Network Traffic Community Deviation
text: Establishing baseline communities of network hosts and identifying statistically divergent inter-community communication.

title: Network Traffic Filtering
text: Restricting network traffic originating from any location.

title: Network Traffic Policy Mapping
text: Network traffic policy mapping identifies and models the allowed pathways of data at the network, transport, and/or application levels.

title: Network Traffic Signature Analysis
text: Analyzing network traffic and compares it to known signatures

title: Network Vulnerability Assessment
text: Network vulnerability assessment relates all the vulnerabilities of a network's components in the context of their configuration and interdependencies and can also include assessing risk emerging from the network's design as a whole, not just the sum of individual network node or network segment vulnerabilities.

title: Null Pointer Checking
text: Checking if a pointer is NULL.

title: OT Variable Access Restriction
text: Assign read/write access controls on designated registers or data tags to prevent unauthorized writes.

title: Object Eviction
text: Terminate or remove an object from a host machine. This is the broadest class for object eviction.

title: One-time Password
text: A one-time password is valid for only one user authentication.

title: Operating Mode Monitoring
text: Detects operating modes such as Program, Run, Remote, or Stop.

title: Operating Mode Restriction
text: Restricting unauthorized changes to the operating mode prevents devices from switching into inappropriate or vulnerable states during normal use.

title: Operating System Monitoring
text: The operating system software, for D3FEND's purposes, includes the kernel and its process management functions, hardware drivers, initialization or boot logic. It also includes and other key system daemons and their configuration. The monitoring or analysis of these components for unauthorized activity constitute **Operating System Monitoring**.

title: Operational Activity Mapping
text: Operational activity mapping identifies activities of the organization and the organization's suborganizations, groups, roles, and individuals that carry out the activities and then establishes the dependencies of the activities on the systems and people that perform those activities.

title: Operational Dependency Mapping
text: Operational dependency mapping identifies and models the dependencies of the organization's activities on each other and on the organization's performers (people, systems, and services.) This may include modeling the higher- and lower-level activities of an organization forming a hierarchy, or layering, of the dependencies in an organization's activities.

title: Operational Logic Validation
text: Validation of variable state in the context of the control logic of the operational application.

title: Operational Process Monitoring
text: Monitoring physical parameters and operator actions related to an operational environment.

title: Operational Risk Assessment
text: Operational risk assessment identifies and models the vulnerabilities of, and risks to, an organization's activities individually and as a whole.

title: Organization Mapping
text: Organization mapping identifies and models the people, roles, and groups with an organization and the relations between them.

title: Outbound Traffic Filtering
text: Restricting network traffic originating from a private host or enclave destined towards untrusted networks.

title: Passive Certificate Analysis
text: Collecting host certificates from network traffic or other passive sources like a certificate transparency log and analyzing them for unauthorized activity.

title: Passive Logical Link Mapping
text: Passive logical link mapping only listens to network traffic as a means to map the the whole data link layer, where the links represent logical data flows rather than physical connections.

title: Password Authentication
text: Password authentication is a security mechanism used to verify the identity of a user or entity attempting to access a system or resource by requiring the input of a secret string of characters, known as a password, that is associated with the user or entity.

title: Password Rotation
text: Password rotation is a security policy that mandates the periodic change of user account passwords to mitigate the risk of unauthorized access due to compromised credentials.

title: Per Host Download-Upload Ratio Analysis
text: Detecting anomalies that indicate malicious activity by comparing the amount of data downloaded versus data uploaded by a host.

title: Peripheral Firmware Verification
text: Cryptographically verifying peripheral firmware integrity.

title: Physical Access Mediation
text: Physical access mediation is the process of granting or denying specific requests to enter specific physical facilities (e.g., Federal buildings, military establishments, border crossing entrances.)

title: Physical Access Monitoring
text: Monitoring the physical access of a specified environment through detection, recording, reviewing, and logging of who/what enters and exists areas.

title: Physical Enclosure Hardening
text: Physical changes to a computer enclosure which reduce the ability for agents or the environment to affect the contained computer system.

title: Physical Link Mapping
text: Physical link mapping identifies and models the link connectivity of the network devices within a physical network.

title: Physical Locking
text: Employ a mechanical locking device for securing moveable portions of physical barriers (e.g., doors, gates, drawers) in a secured position.

title: Platform Hardening
text: Hardening components of a Platform with the intention of making them more difficult to exploit. Platforms includes components such as: * BIOS UEFI Subsystems * Hardware security devices such as Trusted Platform Modules * Boot process logic or code * Kernel software components

title: Platform Monitoring
text: Monitoring platform components such as operating systems software, hardware devices, or firmware.

title: Platform Uptime Monitoring
text: Monitor the amount of time since the last power cycle or restart.

title: Pointer Authentication
text: Comparing the cryptographic hash or derivative of a pointer's value to an expected value.

title: Pointer Validation
text: Ensuring that a pointer variable has the required properties for use.

title: Process Analysis
text: Process Analysis consists of observing a running application process and analyzing it to watch for certain behaviors or conditions which may indicate adversary activity. Analysis can occur inside of the process or through a third-party monitoring application. Examples include monitoring system and privileged calls, monitoring process initiation chains, and memory boundary allocations.

title: Process Code Segment Verification
text: Comparing the "text" or "code" memory segments to a source of truth.

title: Process Eviction
text: Process eviction techniques terminate or remove running process.

title: Process Lineage Analysis
text: Identification of suspicious processes executing on an end-point device by examining the ancestry and siblings of a process, and the associated metadata of each node on the tree, such as process execution, duration, and order relative to siblings and ancestors.

title: Process Segment Execution Prevention
text: Preventing execution of any address in a memory region other than the code segment.

title: Process Self-Modification Detection
text: Detects processes that modify, change, or replace their own code at runtime.

title: Process Spawn Analysis
text: Analyzing spawn arguments or attributes of a process to detect processes that are unauthorized.

title: Process Suspension
text: Suspending a running process on a computer system.

title: Process Termination
text: Terminating a running application process on a computer system.

title: Protocol Metadata Anomaly Detection
text: Collecting network communication protocol metadata and identifying statistical outliers.

title: Proximity Sensor Monitoring
text: Monitoring events from proximity sensors that indicate a credential or tagged asset is within the sensor’s read range or a defined zone. Common enabling technologies include RFID, Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE), and Ultra-Wideband (UWB).

title: Proxy-based Web Server Access Mediation
text: Proxy-based web server access mediation focuses on the regulation of web server access through intermediary proxy servers.

title: RF Shielding
text: Adding physical barriers to a platform to prevent undesired radio interference.

title: RPC Traffic Analysis
text: Monitoring the activity of remote procedure calls in communication traffic to establish standard protocol operations and potential attacker activities.

title: Radiation Hardening
text: Radiation hardening is the process of making electronic components and circuits resistant to damage or malfunction caused by high levels of ionizing radiation.

title: Reference Nullification
text: Invalidating all pointers that reference a specific memory block, ensuring that the block cannot be accessed or modified after deallocation.

title: Registry Key Deletion
text: Delete a registry key.

title: Reissue Credential
text: Issue a new credential to a user which supercedes their old credential.

title: Relay Pattern Analysis
text: The detection of an internal host relaying traffic between the internal network and the external network.

title: Remote File Access Mediation
text: Remote file access mediation is the process of managing and securing access to file systems over a network to ensure that only authorized users or processes can interact with remote files.

title: Remote Firmware Update Monitoring
text: Monitoring of remote firmware update commands to identify unauthorized software installations.

title: Remote Terminal Session Detection
text: Detection of an unauthorized remote live terminal console session by examining network traffic to a network host.

title: Resource Access Pattern Analysis
text: Analyzing the resources accessed by a user to identify unauthorized activity.

title: Restore Access
text: Restoring an entity's access to resources.

title: Restore Configuration
text: Restoring an software configuration.

title: Restore Database
text: Restoring the data in a database.

title: Restore Disk Image
text: Restoring a previously captured disk image a hard drive.

title: Restore Email
text: Restoring an email for an entity to access.

title: Restore File
text: Restoring a file for an entity to access.

title: Restore Network Access
text: Restoring a entity's access to a computer network.

title: Restore Object
text: Restoring an object for an entity to access. This is the broadest class for object restoral.

title: Restore Software
text: Restoring software to a host.

title: Restore User Account Access
text: Restoring a user account's access to resources.

title: Reverse Resolution IP Denylisting
text: Blocking a reverse lookup based on the query's IP address value.

title: Routing Access Mediation
text: Routing access mediation is a network security approach that manages and controls access at the network layer using VPNs, tunneling protocols, firewall rules, and traffic inspection to ensure secure and efficient data routing.

title: Scheduled Job Analysis
text: Analysis of source files, processes, destination files, or destination servers associated with a scheduled job to detect unauthorized use of job scheduling.

title: Script Execution Analysis
text: Analyzing the execution of a script to detect unauthorized user activity.

title: Segment Address Offset Randomization
text: Randomizing the base (start) address of one or more segments of memory during the initialization of a process.

title: Sender MTA Reputation Analysis
text: Characterizing the reputation of mail transfer agents (MTA) to determine the security risk in emails.

title: Sender Reputation Analysis
text: Ascertaining sender reputation based on information associated with a message (e.g. email/instant messaging).

title: Service Binary Verification
text: Analyzing changes in service binary files by comparing to a source of truth.

title: Service Dependency Mapping
text: Service dependency mapping determines the services on which each given service relies.

title: Session Duration Analysis
text: Analyzing the duration of user sessions in order to detect unauthorized activity.

title: Session Termination
text: Forcefully end all active sessions associated with compromised accounts or devices.

title: Shadow Stack Comparisons
text: Comparing a call stack in system memory with a shadow call stack maintained by the processor to determine unauthorized shellcode activity.

title: Software Inventory
text: Software inventorying identifies and records the software items in the organization's architecture.

title: Software Update
text: Replacing old software on a computer system component.

title: Source Code Hardening
text: Hardening source code with the intention of making it more difficult to exploit and less error prone.

title: Stack Frame Canary Validation
text: Comparing a value stored in a stack frame with a known good value in order to prevent or detect a memory segment overwrite.

title: Standalone Honeynet
text: An environment created for the purpose of attracting attackers and eliciting their behaviors that is not connected to any production enterprise systems.

title: Strong Password Policy
text: Modifying system configuration to increase password strength.

title: System Call Analysis
text: Analyzing system calls to determine whether a process is exhibiting unauthorized behavior.

title: System Call Filtering
text: Controlling access to local computer system resources with kernel-level capabilities.

title: System Configuration Permissions
text: Restricting system configuration modifications to a specific user or group of users.

title: System Daemon Monitoring
text: Tracking changes to the state or configuration of critical system level processes.

title: System Dependency Mapping
text: System dependency mapping identifies and models the dependencies of system components on each other to carry out their function.

title: System File Analysis
text: Monitoring system files such as authentication databases, configuration files, system logs, and system executables for modification or tampering.

title: System Firmware Verification
text: Cryptographically verifying installed system firmware integrity.

title: System Init Config Analysis
text: Analysis of any system process startup configuration.

title: System Mapping
text: System mapping encompasses the techniques to identify the organization's systems, how they are configured and decomposed into subsystems and components, how they are dependent on one another, and where they are physically located.

title: System Vulnerability Assessment
text: System vulnerability assessment relates all the vulnerabilities of a system's components in the context of their configuration and internal dependencies and can also include assessing risk emerging from the system's design as a whole, not just the sum of individual component vulnerabilities.

title: TPM Boot Integrity
text: Assuring the integrity of a platform by demonstrating that the boot process starts from a trusted combination of hardware and software and continues until the operating system has fully booted and applications are running. Sometimes called Static Root of Trust Measurement (STRM).

title: Token-based Authentication
text: Token-based authentication is an authentication protocol where users verify their identity in exchange for a unique access token. Users can then access the website, application, or resource for the life of the token without having to re-enter their credentials.

title: Token Binding
text: Token binding is a security mechanism used to enhance the protection of tokens, such as cookies or OAuth tokens, by binding them to a specific connection.

title: Transfer Agent Authentication
text: Validating that server components of a messaging infrastructure are authorized to send a particular message.

title: Trusted Library
text: A trusted library is a collection of pre-verified and secure code modules or components that are used within software applications to perform specific functions. These libraries are considered reliable and have been vetted for security vulnerabilities, ensuring they do not introduce risks into the application.

title: URL Analysis
text: Determining if a URL is benign or malicious by analyzing the URL or its components.

title: URL Reputation Analysis
text: Analyzing the reputation of a URL.

title: Unlock Account
text: Restoring a user account's access to resources by unlocking a locked User Account.

title: User Account Permissions
text: Restricting a user account's access to resources.

title: User Behavior Analysis
text: User behavior analytics ("UBA") as defined by Gartner, is a cybersecurity process about detection of insider threats, targeted attacks, and financial fraud. UBA solutions look at patterns of human behavior, and then apply algorithms and statistical analysis to detect meaningful anomalies from those patterns-anomalies that indicate potential threats.' Instead of tracking devices or security events, UBA tracks a system's users. Big data platforms are increasing UBA functionality by allowing them to analyze petabytes worth of data to detect insider threats and advanced persistent threats.

title: User Data Transfer Analysis
text: Analyzing the amount of data transferred by a user.

title: User Geolocation Logon Pattern Analysis
text: Monitoring geolocation data of user logon attempts and comparing it to a baseline user behavior profile to identify anomalies in logon location.

title: User Group Permissions
text: Access control where access is determined based on attributes associated with users and the objects being accessed.

title: User Session Init Config Analysis
text: Analyzing modifications to user session config files such as .bashrc or .bash_profile.

title: Variable Initialization
text: Setting variables to a known value before use.

title: Variable Type Validation
text: Ensuring that a variable has the correct type.

title: Video Surveillance
text: Monitoring of physical areas via camera video feeds to deter, detect, and investigate unauthorized access and related security events.

title: Web Session Access Mediation
text: Web session access mediation secures user sessions in web applications by employing robust authentication and integrity validation, along with adaptive threat mitigation techniques, to ensure that access to web resources is authorized and protected from session-related attacks.

title: Web Session Activity Analysis
text: Monitoring changes in user web session behavior by comparing current web session activity to a baseline behavior profile or a catalog of predetermined malicious behavior.
